title: Ram Charittar Upadhyay v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Krishna Murari, J.; Ajay Bhanot, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner left to Clause 6.5 bill-accuracy remedy.
headnote: A writ challenging the correctness and accuracy of an electricity consumption bill is not entertainable. The consumer has a statutory alternative remedy of approaching the competent authority under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Ram Charittar Upadhyay filed Writ-C No. 8168 of 2018 in the Allahabad High Court challenging the correctness and accuracy of a bill for consumption of electrical energy. The State of Uttar Pradesh and four others were arrayed as respondents; counsel for respondents 3 to 5 appeared. The Division Bench heard the matter on 5 March 2018. The consumer invoked writ jurisdiction rather than the Supply Code machinery for billing disputes.

holding_units.holding: A writ petition challenging the correctness and accuracy of a bill for consumption of electrical energy is not liable to be entertained, because Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 gives the consumer a statutory alternative remedy of approaching the competent authority in a dispute over accuracy of the bill; the petition was dismissed, leaving it open to the petitioner to avail that remedy.

not_decided.point: Correctness and accuracy of the impugned electricity bill
not_decided.note: Writ not entertained on the alternative-remedy bar; merits of the bill left open for Clause 6.5.
